decisions.executionNote: Wait with both arms stationary and open for the opponent's discard.
Continue waiting while the opponent approaches its tiles.
Keep clear until the opponent has exposed and released the discard.
Observe the tile as the opponent finishes pushing it face up.
The discard shows two circles, matching the middle three tiles. Begin a gradual elbow-up left-arm approach while the opponent retracts.
Approach the leftmost matching two-circle tile, keeping the left elbow raised and the right arm stationary.
Align above the first matching tile and close the empty gripper to make a narrow pusher, avoiding neighboring upright tiles.
Gently tip the leftmost two-circle tile away from the robot with a narrow closed-gripper push.
Finish the first gentle push and allow the matching tile to settle face up before withdrawing.
Withdraw from the first tipped tile, then shift above the second matching tile without touching its neighbors.
Push only the second two-circle tile forward and down, using the closed gripper as a narrow pusher.
The second matching tile is down. Withdraw left and begin the right-arm elbow-up approach to the third, keeping the arms on their own sides.
Clear the center with the left arm while advancing the right gripper above the remaining matching tile, maintaining smooth elbow-up configurations.
Finish aligning the right closed-gripper pusher above the third two-circle tile while the left arm continues clearing the row.
Gently push the third matching two-circle tile down with the right closed gripper, leaving the nonmatching row upright.
Allow the third tile to settle and withdraw the right pusher. Move the left arm toward the side stack for the kong replacement draw.
Align the left open gripper over the top near tile of the side stack; lift the right arm clear of the declared tiles.
Lower the left gripper around the near top stack tile. Begin orienting the raised right gripper for a later transfer, clear of the row.
Close around the stack tile and lift cautiously, checking visible retention; continue the right wrist's gradual transfer orientation.
The stack tile is visibly retained. Carry it inward above the row while gradually rotating for the handoff; keep both elbows up.
Continue carrying the retained replacement tile toward the center handoff, with the right gripper open and clear.
Set the held tile at the central handoff orientation and stabilize before the right gripper approaches its exposed edge.
Bring the right gripper around the held tile's exposed edge and begin closing, while the left hand holds still.
Secure the tile with the right gripper, release the left, and separate slowly to verify the handoff visually.
The right hand visibly retains the tile. Clear the left arm and begin a smooth outward carry to the open right end of the row.
Carry the replacement tile toward the row's right end with a gradual wrist rotation, while withdrawing the empty left arm.
Continue the retained tile outward above the nonmatching row, maintaining clearance before the final placement descent.
Raise the held tile clear of the row and finish orienting above the right-end placement. Some neighboring tiles appear tilted and will need checking.
Lower the retained replacement tile vertically at the right end, avoiding further lateral contact with the row.
Set the replacement tile down at the right end and open the gripper, then inspect the row for needed corrections.
Withdraw the open right gripper upward and back to inspect and recover the fallen nonmatching tile without disturbing the placed tile.
Replan from the interrupted pose with half-size increments, lifting and backing away from the row before tile recovery.
Approach above the fallen nonmatching tile in front of the right row, rotating the open gripper for a narrow side grasp.
Align the right gripper above the face-down nonmatching tile, keeping clear of the neighboring upright tiles.
Lower the open right gripper toward the fallen tile's sides with a small leftward alignment correction.
Settle the right fingers beside the face-down tile and close slowly for a recovery grasp.
Lift the recovery grasp vertically to confirm the fallen nonmatching tile is retained before standing it back up.
The recovery tile is retained. Rotate it toward upright above the table while moving forward for clearance.
Continue the slow upright rotation with the tile held clear of the table and nearby tiles.
Finish orienting the recovered nonmatching tile vertically and align it above the empty part of the row.
Lower the upright recovery tile toward its vacant row position, with small forward and lateral corrections.
Make a small visual alignment correction so the recovered tile stands in line with the two undisturbed neighbors.
Release the recovered tile upright, then lift the open fingers straight clear of its neighbors.
Withdraw the empty right hand upward and back to inspect the upright tiles and the kong group without contact.
Move the open right arm to a clear inspection pose, keeping the elbow configuration continuous.
The row tiles now appear upright. Approach above the displaced matching tile to turn its green back face down and join the other two.
Align the open right gripper above the green-backed displaced tile, staying on the right side of the workspace.
Descend slowly around the displaced green-backed tile for a side grasp, keeping clear of the opponent's upright tiles.
Use the wrist view to advance the open fingers toward the displaced tile's center before closing.
Close gently around the displaced tile after lowering the fingers to its sides.
Lift and draw the grasped tile clear of the opponent's row before changing its orientation.
The tile slipped during the lift. Reopen and correct backward and downward to center the fingers on its sides.
Use the unobstructed wrist view to center the displaced tile and approach its side edges more precisely.
Lower around the centered tile's sidewalls and close for a deeper, more secure grasp.
Lift vertically with the gripper closed and verify retention before any further rotation.
The tile is now retained. Raise it for clearance and begin a slow rotation toward upright before tipping it face up.
Continue rotating the retained matching tile toward upright while compensating its position to keep it clear of the table.
Replan after the continuity stop: move the retained tile slightly right and back without rotation to regain joint margin.
With joint margin restored, finish the upright rotation while lifting and moving back into clear tabletop space.
Move into clear space in front of the row and tilt the retained tile past upright toward white-face-up placement.
The held tile is confirmed as two circles. Lower it close to the tabletop while tilting further toward a face-up resting position.
